title: ChatBridge translation layer: deterministic mapping from OpenAI Chat semantics to Redwood structured-output v2
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Redwood supports a structured-output v2 envelope and first-class function/tool calling. Many customers have clients and legacy integrations that speak the OpenAI Chat Completions API. We need a deterministic adapter that maps OpenAI-style request/response shapes (including streaming SSE/HTTP2 fragments, nested function/tool call events, and legacy role/name patterns) into Redwood's canonical internal format and back out.

Goals: Ensure parity for functional behavior (function/tool invocation, tool-call arguments, function return handling, content filters), preserve observability signals (token boundaries, chunk IDs, latency), and avoid breaking customer-side idempotency or retry semantics. The adapter must support both streaming (SSE + chunked HTTP2) and non-streaming modes and maintain correct structured-output typing.

Constraints and non-goals: We are not attempting to emulate historical OpenAI server-side behaviors (e.g., undocumented backoff heuristics). We will not change upstream SDKs. Edge-case backward-compatibility for malformed legacy clients is out-of-scope for this ticket and will be handled by follow-ups.

Design approach (summary):
- Request mapping: translate OpenAI chat roles (system/user/assistant) and message arrays into Redwood request.envelope with explicit conversation_id, turn_id, and a request_id. Preserve client-provided message.name where present. Normalize content field into Redwood.declarations.content and capture any top-level options (max_tokens, temperature) under Redwood.config.
- Streaming: map OpenAI SSE/stream "delta" events into Redwood framed tokens with a stable chunk_id and sequence number. Attach a small header object in the first chunk for metadata (model variant, request_id) and subsequent chunks carry token patches and function-call fragments. For HTTP2 streaming we preserve frame boundaries and include a reorder buffer to avoid duplicate-delivery semantics on replays.
- Function/tool calling: when OpenAI semantics emit a single function call in streaming mode (with multiple deltas for name and arguments), the adapter will assemble the complete call before injecting a Redwood.tool_invocation event. If the client requests early function invocation (explicit streaming tool invocation flag), the adapter will emit progressive tool_invocation.partial events with deterministic reconciliation rules.
- Structured outputs: Redwood structured-output v2 uses typed 'outcome' envelopes. We will map OpenAI 'choices[*].message' and 'choices[*].finish_reason' into outcome.type (e.g., 'message', 'function_call', 'end_of_stream') and outcome.payload with schema markers. All stringified JSON arguments from OpenAI function calls will be parsed when valid JSON; on parse errors we include a structured parse_error field rather than silently failing.

Key mapping table (excerpt):
- OpenAI request: {"model","messages","functions","max_tokens","stream"} -> Redwood request: {"model_alias","conversation.messages[]","toolset","limits.max_tokens","streaming.enabled"}
- OpenAI message: {"role","content","name"} -> Redwood.message: {"role_kind","body","sender_name","meta.client_name"}
- OpenAI choice.finish_reason "function_call" -> Redwood.outcome.type "tool_call_initiated"

Acceptance criteria (must pass all):
1) Unit tests: request/response mapping deterministic tests for 12 representative message patterns (simple chat, multi-function turn, nested function args, streaming with interleaved tool fragments).
2) Integration tests: end-to-end against the local compat harness that asserts token-level ordering, reconstructed function argument JSON equality, and structured-output schema conformance.
3) Streaming conformance: adapter must replay an SSE stream with reordered arrival and produce identical reconstructed output (idempotent-when-replayed).
4) Observability: token-level telemetry emitted with request_id and chunk_id; latency histograms for first-byte and last-byte on streaming responses.
5) Backwards compatibility: existing Redwood hosted API keys that used the legacy mapping must not observe regressions in error codes for a curated regression suite.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (canary): deploy adapter behind a toggle for 5% of traffic; collect mismatch rate and error deltas in canary logs.
- Phase B (graded ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 75% over 48h windows with automated rollback on error rate > 1% above baseline.
- Phase C: full rollout with observability retention and a postmortem checklist.

Telemetry & metrics to add:
- compat.mapping.mismatch_count (by kind: role, function_args, streaming_reorder)
- compat.streaming.chunk_delay_ms P50/P95
- compat.toolcall.assembly_time_ms
- compat.parse_error.rate

Migration notes for SDK teams: provide a short doc with mapping equivalence tables and example payloads (sample requests and sample streaming sequences) in Confluence.

Security and privacy considerations: redact PII from message bodies for telemetry; do not log full function argument JSON except under debug traces with customer consent.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Triage: flagged P1 due to enterprise demand for consistent OpenAI compatibility. Assigned to Alejandro for scoping.
2026-02-18 - Design review notes: Design WG asked to clarify partial function-call behavior for streaming; decided on assembly-then-emit by default with an opt-in progressive partial mode.

2026-02-24 - Engineering update: Prototype implemented for non-streaming mapping. Basic tests pass for simple chat and single function call flows. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4821

2026-03-02 - QA note: Found edge cases where clients send 'name' on assistant messages (rare) which previously caused role inversion. Added normalizer to preserve explicit name and not overwrite role_kind.
2026-03-07 - UX/Docs: Drafted Confluence doc with example mappings and streaming diagrams: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMPAT/pages/ChatBridge+Mapping

2026-03-10 - Integration: Streaming harness run against 500 recorded OpenAI sessions. Observed 0.8% benign mismatches related to whitespace normalization in function args; added canonical-whitespace normalization step.
Pending: Need security review for debug-level argument logging flow and toggle that requires customer opt-in.
